steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: ...From dream's deep, return; by light's edge, the gates unseal... From dream's—

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Oh, you're finally awake... Settle!

Your eyes are forced open, yet the cold mist of the dream still clings to you, seeping through your skin. Only when something pokes your forehead again—insistent, familiar—does consciousness begin to trickle back.
Lichen is right there, her eyes meeting yours. You grasp her sleeve. Your grip tightens, and your hand slides down until you find her wrist—warmth, pulse, the steady rhythm of life.
She pauses, startled by your desperation, then reaches out to feel your forehead before finally letting out a sigh of relief.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: You were gone so long this time. Even the Yin fish lost its thread halfway... You really had me worried.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: What happened?
She looks you up and down, but can't find what she's searching for.
I think it should be fine.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: When?! Did she do something to you?
But the little fish swam over to her. So I don't have it on me now.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Whew... I was afraid she'd try to keep you there again like last time...
You shake your head.
I didn't ask anything I shouldn't have. So she didn't ask anything of me.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Ah... Well done, young friend. Smart and steady. That puts my mind at ease.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: But how did the Yin fish end up with my shifu...? Did she subdue it, or...

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Given where things stand now, can we still use the Yang fish to trace it...?

Seeing you safe, she relaxes, shoulders softening. Then, as if flipping a switch, she resumes counting on her fingers, muttering under her breath. Her face cycles through expressions: puzzlement, concentration, and the occasional furrow of deep thought.
You watch her for a while, taking in her ever-shifting yet radiant expressions. At last, you break the silence.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Hmm?
I don't think I know you as well as I should. Tell me about your shifu.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Hmm... To be honest, my memory's a little blurry. I wasn't that old when she left, and it's been so long. What I remember best is getting scolded whenever I got into trouble.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: I am grateful she predicted the Perishing Star, though. I didn't believe her at the time, but she kept me pinned at home the day of the Nightfall. At least that spared me the worst of it.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Oh, did I never mention? Shifu is actually a distant relative of mine. The Tianyi Sect? Family business. Kept behind closed doors, just between us.
Lichen winks at you. You open your mouth to speak, but the words catch in your throat. It takes a moment before you finally manage to ask:
...Did it hurt? Letting her go?

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: It was alright. Grief comes, grief goes. Those who seek the Dao learn to let go. Every year on her death anniversary, I bring some treats to her grave and let her have a sniff. Filial enough, I think. As for mourning... I'm nothing compared to her fans online.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Honestly? I think Shifu suffered more from her prophecies than anything. When the Perishing Star came, and she lost her mind... in a way, it was a mercy.

Is it the Eastian way? Or simply the mark of a generation that knew how to let things go? Life and death and parting—she touches each one with such gentleness, such ease, as though they were ordinary as morning light. And suddenly your own sorrow feels like a stone you have carried too long.
I thought... you couldn't let go. That's why you pushed yourself to come here. To bring her back...
Your words amuse her. A soft laugh escapes, and then she's sweeping you into her arms, holding you tight. Her hand finds your hair and ruffles it with reckless affection.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: You are worried about me? Oh, you—such a good kid! So precious!
Hey...! Stop messing my hair up!

After a bit of playful tussling, she finally stills. But she doesn't let you go. Instead, she draws you closer, tucking you into her arms for warmth. Her chin comes to rest atop your head, and together, you gaze out at the hazy ruins in the distance.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Truth be told, my Daoist arts aren't all that refined. My divination's barely accurate. I prefer the odd and unconventional, all in good fun, never digging too deep. Forget comparing me to Shifu; I might not even outdo that copper coin of yours.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: It was only after the Perishing Star fell that my hodgepodge arts slowly started working. More convincing by the day. More people came seeking help. Bit by bit... I actually became a proper Daoist.
Was it the shift in the Mania field that triggered her awakening? Her Mania power? Though she'd probably never heard of it.

options: Because the Perishing Star changed the Dao of Heaven?

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: There's a theory that says the great calamity threw heaven and earth out of balance—Yin and Yang in chaos, evil spirits running wild. That's what gave my unorthodox methods power. Enough to overwhelm the orthodox ones.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: There's some truth to it. But it's too stiff. I don't care for such a lifeless explanation.

options: Then what do you think it is...?

steps.content: She gazes into the distance, her eyes growing ever more pensive.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: I believe the Daoist arts make no distinction between righteous and wicked, good and evil. The Dao of Heaven is chaos; we'll never be able to fully grasp it. Arts that fulfill the wishes of the believers... those are good arts.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: ...And what <color=#fb9259>people believe in</color> will have power.
You pause, struck by her words.
Yes. You have heard this theory before. Not in DisCity. Not from anything resembling science.
But somewhere far from here and now—nearly a century later, thousands of miles away in <color=#fb9259>Eastia</color>—someone, it seems, has proven it true.

steps.speaker: Du Ruo
steps.content: Hypercubes don't exist in Eastia. Facing the Apostle, people could only rely on their faith in the Sun Shot legend. In other words, they were fighting the product of collective will with their collective will.

steps.speaker: Du Ruo
steps.content: When the Great Seer crafted the Almighty Bow, she was activating this immense spiritual power. No matter how many times she failed, she always had that faith. This, Yanyan is surely capable of.

options: Is this wisdom from the Eastern Continent?

steps.content: She smiles and waves the question away.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Figured it out myself. Haven't published a paper yet.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Before the Nightfall, even with all the conflict and war, people still clung to "science." Those who came to me or my shifu were mostly looking for entertainment. No one truly believed in the Daoist arts, so the arts never took hold.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: But after the Nightfall, everything changed.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: That baleful star, and everything it brought, could neither be explained nor stopped. Science, common sense, all of it useless. Everything people once believed in was uprooted and swept away. And in its place, irrational faith captured their attention.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Praying to gods. Worshipping Buddha. Embracing the supernatural. The more mysterious and incomprehensible, the better. That way, the slightest miracle could be taken as divine intervention, a flicker of hope.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: ...As if believing in something—finding the right method, praying to the right being—could restore the world to its former grace. As if what was lost might still return.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: You see, fortune and misfortune go hand in hand. It was that sorrowful faith that granted our arts their power.

In this silent, labyrinthine city, the two of you are barely more than specks, adrift among endless stone corridors. Yet when you look up at her, you see it: the vast heavens, the twisted stars, the whole sprawling cosmos reflected in her eyes.
Then her smile fades. Her gaze sharpens, unbent by anyone or anything. She is looking at something you cannot see. Something far beyond.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: That is why I must see my shifu. She has become an icon to hundreds of followers, and they hope she will truly rise from the dead, just as they long for their own loved ones to return.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: And if... my shifu can truly return from the Void of Yin, then the path I seek will finally have its answer.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: And you, young friend, would no longer have to fear losing anyone.

You watch her. You cannot stop watching her—those cyan eyes, the small mole between her brows, the gentle curve of her smile. You keep watching until your knuckles blanch white. Until your nails bite crescents into your palms.
She notices. Gently, she pries your fingers open. Only then do you feel the sharp, waking pain of flesh remembering itself.
You look away.
...The place you're going is really dangerous. Aren't you afraid at all?
It's too dangerous. It's really dangerous there. I don't want you to go. What if you run into something even your divination can't foresee?

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Cross each bridge as it comes. I've studied so many mystical arts precisely to have more ways to handle situations like this.

options: What if those don't work either?

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Then I'll adapt and wait for the right moment. The path will reveal itself when the time comes. I'm patient; I can wait for my chance to act.

options: What if the path never reveals itself?

steps.content: What if you actually die this time?
What if all your resolve means nothing?
Your barrage of questions comes like stones cast into still water, but her smile does not ripple.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Then that, too, shall be my destiny, a fate I've sealed with my own hands.
As if sensing the weight her words would carry, she pulls you closer the moment she finishes speaking, still smiling.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: It's not so frightening, really. Don't let appearances fool you. This humble Daoist is more meticulous than she seems. I've made all the necessary preparations. Look—
[Big CG 02]

She tucks a strand of stray hair behind her ear, and in the same motion, an Eastian rune drifts lazily through the air before hooking itself onto her earlobe. With her peculiar arts, she has made herself a curious little earring.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Artifacts, talismans... I've got plenty more on me. Enough to save my life several times over! And with you, my auspicious star, by my side? Everything will be just fine.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Once I meet my shifu, I'll kneel and pay my respects properly. While I'm at it, I'll put in a good word for you—

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: You've helped me so much on this journey, young friend. Perhaps you could earn yourself the title of "honorary disciple"? Then I would be your senior.

She beams with pride, tilting her head to invite you to touch this little creation of hers. Her smile is radiant, like sunlight breaking through a century of clouds, warming you where you stand. A moment you will carry forever.
But you don't reach out.
You don't dare.

...You fear that the instant your fingers meet her, she will dissolve. That the boundary between dream and reality will shatter, and you will fall back into that other space, that other time, so recently visited, where you truly touched something. And it was not this.
[Big CG 03-04]

You have reached out before. You have truly touched her face. In the depths of that lonely darkness, the sensation traveled through your fingertips—cold, rigid, immovable—and pierced straight into your heart like a shard of ice.

It could only be the body of someone long dead. A hollow shell, her soul long scattered, held together only by runes sprawling across her form, dark Eastian Daoist arts pulsing beneath the skin. You know who cast the spell.

—Only one person would so arrogantly trample the boundaries of life and death. Only one would so cruelly enslave the remains of the departed. Only one would so mercilessly... deny even herself any peace.
You know what your palm touched was real. You know this is how her story ends. And yet, the questions only multiply—
How did it come to this?

Was she lost in the ruins, no way forward, no way back? Did Shin's whispers lure her into the abyss? Or did the forbidden path demand too much? Too many questions. Too many answers. Until the price came due.

Now adrift in this cold tide of death, what does she feel? Is she still that same girl, open-hearted and free-spirited, as you remember? Or has she become like the countless phantoms she once guided onward? Lost, anguished, lingering without end. Does she know now? That her pursuit of transcending life and death was nothing but a fool's dream, even after a hundred years? That the path she sought was merely a tiny flicker of light beneath the boundless night sky, gone in an instant, as though it never was?
All her life, she read the signs and asked the heavens. She believed in omens, in fate, in you—her auspicious star. So before she began this long journey—
Did she already know how it would end?
...And if she knew, did she still choose to walk toward it?
—These are questions you must not ask. You know the rules of the Void of Yin. <color=#fb9259>Offer no glance to the departed. Lend no ear to the abyss. Speak no question to the spirits.</color>
But even so... even so...
Is there still time... for me to do something for you?
Her lifeless eyes lifted slightly, meeting yours for a moment before lowering again. A soft chuckle escaped her.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Heh...
You spoke after all, breaking the taboo. Yet, fortunately, no punishment came.
It seemed, that time, even the Void of Yin had no answer to give.
[Return to the Surface World]
A cool breeze sweeps through you, clearing the haze from your thoughts. You come back to your senses just as Lichen shivers before you, her eyes lighting up.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Ah, I've found the Yin fish. It's near. Will you stay here, or come with me, young friend?

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: The trouble yonder seems still for now, and I'm rested. Either way, I can take you with me, or leave a ward for your keeping.

In the distance, dark mist rolls in like tidal waves, devouring the light above you inch by inch. Your tiny shadows are swallowed whole. The paths through the ruins twist and turn, just as chaotic as fate's crossroads.
Lichen has already risen. She gazes toward the road ahead, the one that was always waiting for her.
She looks just as she did long ago, sitting by her window, watching distant mountains burn, watching endless incense smoke curl at her doorstep.
...But you cannot accept it. Not yet. Not this.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Ah, that gladdens me even more. The elders in my sect always said a restless soul like mine would surely bring some calamity one day, if left unwatched.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Hehe, but those fools never saw that I would meet you, young friend.
She crouches before you, taking your hands in hers. Your fingertips meet, warmth against warmth.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: If I do wander too far, just call my name. Whenever you call, I will answer.
As your fingers part, delicate threads of light linger between your fingertips. For one heart-stopping instant, they hold, and then they scatter, dissolving into the air like an illusion.

steps.speaker: Lichen
steps.content: Fear not. I will return to you.
You answer her in the silence of your heart.
—You will. I will bring you back.
